rows.name: Sync files on save
rows.offer: Compose Watch copies edited host files into the running service container so a hot-reload framework picks them up without a rebuild.

rows.name: Rebuild image on file change
rows.offer: Compose Watch can rebuild the image with BuildKit and replace the container when chosen files, such as a dependency manifest, change.

flisk.reason: Tilt rebuilds images when watched sources change, but the paths that trigger a rebuild are not configurable per service in service.json.

rows.name: Per-path watch actions
rows.offer: Compose lets each watched path choose sync, rebuild, sync with restart, or sync followed by a custom command, with ignore patterns.

flisk.reason: Developers on config-heavy services want to restart or run a command on one file change, which fits the Tilt live_update Flisk already generates.

rows.acceptance: service.json gains a watch block (sync paths, ignore, restart/exec action) that runtime/engine turns into live_update steps; proven by a field in runtime/engine/schemas/service-schema.json plus a text check in docs/service-json.md.

ice.basis: Impact 5: fixes slow reloads on non-hot-reload runtimes. Confidence 7: the Compose reference documents the actions and Tilt live_update has run and restart steps. Ease 4: needs schema, engine and drift-check changes in runtime/engine.

rows.name: Start a subset of services
rows.offer: Compose profiles mark optional services so they start only when their profile is enabled by flag or environment variable.

rows.name: Include other project files
rows.offer: The include element pulls another Compose file in as a building block with its own project directory, so teams own their part of a big app.

flisk.reason: Flisk discovers service.json manifests under several scan roots, but it cannot pull in another project's manifest set by reference.

rows.name: Extend shared service config
rows.offer: The extends attribute lets one service reuse and override a common service definition from the same or another file.

flisk.reason: Teams with many near-identical services would avoid copy-pasted service.json; the manifest is plain JSON so a reference field could fit.

rows.acceptance: A service.json field (for example extends) is accepted by runtime/engine/schemas/service-schema.json and resolved by runtime/discovery, shown by a docs/service-json.md section and a passing flisk config verify.

ice.basis: Impact 4: convenience for larger monorepos, not a blocker. Confidence 6: clear Compose feature but few asks seen from agent-stack users. Ease 4: needs schema plus discovery normalization work.

rows.name: Layer override files per environment
rows.offer: Several Compose files can be merged in order so a base file is overridden for dev, test or admin tasks.

flisk.reason: Flisk switches environment through a different project env file but not by layering manifest overrides.

rows.name: Wait for healthy dependencies
rows.offer: depends_on with a health condition starts a service only after its dependency reports healthy, not merely running.

rows.name: Dependency runs to completion first
rows.offer: The service_completed_successfully condition holds a service back until a one-shot dependency such as a migration exits cleanly.

rows.name: Declare AI models as dependencies
rows.offer: A models top-level element declares which LLMs an app needs, runs them through Docker Model Runner, and injects each model's URL and name as environment variables.

flisk.reason: Local agent stacks nearly always need a model endpoint, and a model resource that injects URL and name into dependents fits the agent resource type.

rows.acceptance: A resource type or service.json block for a local model is accepted by the schema, started by flisk up, and listed by flisk status and the resource_list MCP tool, with URL and model env vars documented in docs/service-json.md.

ice.basis: Impact 6: the launch audience builds agent systems that need a local model, and today they hand-wire one as bring-your-own. Confidence 6: the Compose page is clear, but Model Runner is Docker-specific and Ollama is common. Ease 3: needs a new resource kind across schema, engine and doctor.

rows.name: Platform capability provider services
rows.offer: Provider services let a Compose service declare a platform capability that a plugin or binary provisions and whose connection details are injected into dependents.

flisk.reason: Flisk can run any local process or image as a bring-your-own resource, but there is no plugin hook that provisions a capability and injects its variables.

text.contains: Runs the service as a local process

rows.name: Convert Compose to Kubernetes
rows.offer: Compose Bridge turns a Compose model into Kubernetes manifests and a Kustomize overlay using customizable transformation templates.

flisk.reason: Flisk is local-only and its roadmap says it is not a Kubernetes tool.

rows.name: Publish apps as OCI artifacts
rows.offer: docker compose publish pushes a Compose application to an OCI registry so others can run it straight from the registry.

flisk.reason: Flisk projects are shared through version control and the roadmap rules out production deploy and shipping generated Compose files.

rows.name: GPU device reservations
rows.offer: A service can reserve host GPU devices through the deploy device settings with capabilities, count or device ids.

flisk.reason: Local model and agent services often need a GPU on Linux hosts, and the setting would pass through to the generated Compose service.

rows.acceptance: service.json accepts a gpu setting that appears in the generated Compose file and is listed in docs/service-json.md; flisk doctor checks the NVIDIA runtime.

ice.basis: Impact 4: only Linux or Windows GPU hosts benefit and Docker Desktop on Mac cannot. Confidence 6: the Compose page is clear. Ease 3: schema, Compose template and a doctor check all change.

rows.name: Secrets mounted as files
rows.offer: Compose mounts each secret as a file under /run/secrets so values stay out of environment variables and logs.

flisk.reason: Flisk keeps secret values out of generated files and masks them in logs, but injects them as environment variables rather than mounted files.

text.contains: Injected by Compose from the project `.env`

rows.name: Post-start and pre-stop hooks
rows.offer: Lifecycle hooks run a command right after a container starts or just before it stops, optionally with elevated privileges.

flisk.reason: Seeding data after a service is up is common in local stacks, though migrators already cover the most frequent case.

rows.acceptance: service.json accepts a postStart command that runs after the container reports healthy, documented in docs/service-json.md and visible in flisk logs.

ice.basis: Impact 4: migrator resources already cover migrations. Confidence 5: Compose use is clear but demand in Flisk issues is unverified. Ease 3: needs engine ordering work in runtime/engine.

rows.name: Share base layers across images
rows.offer: Compose docs show multi-stage Dockerfiles and a shared base target so many service images reuse the same layers.

rows.name: Env files and interpolation
rows.offer: Compose resolves variables from env files, the shell and the file itself in a documented order, and the CLI can take an alternate env file.

rows.name: Named projects side by side
rows.offer: A project name namespaces containers, networks and volumes so several copies of one app can run on the same host.

flisk.reason: Flisk plans collision-free host ports so two stacks can coexist, but there is no flag to name or clone a project's runtime.

rows.name: Service discovery by name
rows.offer: Compose puts all services on a default network where each is reachable by its service name.

rows.name: Run commands in a service
rows.offer: docker compose exec and run execute a command in a running or fresh service container.

flisk.reason: Users and agents often need a quick shell or script inside a service, and Flisk only offers logs, restart and status.

rows.acceptance: A command (for example flisk exec <resource> -- <cmd>) exists in cli/src/commands and an MCP tool in cli/src/mcp/tools.ts, proven by a command evidence entry and an mcpTool entry.

ice.basis: Impact 5: the first thing a user reaches for after up, and agents benefit too. Confidence 7: exec and run are core Compose commands. Ease 4: needs resource-to-container resolution for both Docker and local-process modes.

rows.name: Wait until services are healthy
rows.offer: docker compose up --wait blocks until services are running or healthy, which scripts and CI use as a readiness gate.

text.contains: when the stack is ready or the command fails

rows.name: Logs and service status
rows.offer: Compose streams service logs and lists service status from the command line.

rows.name: Throwaway test environments
rows.offer: Compose can create and destroy an isolated environment for an automated test suite in CI.
